arXiv:1306.2842v3 [math.AP] 06 Mar 2014

On the global regularity of two-dimensional generalized magnetohydrodynamics systemThanks: The author expresses gratitude to Professor Jiahong Wu and Professor David Ullrich for their teaching.

Kazuo Yamazaki
Abstract.

We study the two-dimensional generalized magnetohydrodynamics system with dissipation and diffusion in terms of fractional Laplacians. In particular, we show that in case the diffusion term has the power β=1\beta=1, in contrast to the previous result of α≥12\alpha\geq\frac{1}{2}, we show that α>13\alpha>\frac{1}{3} suffices in order for the solution pair of velocity and magnetic fields to remain smooth for all time.

Keywords: Global regularity, magnetohydrodynamics system, Navier-Stokes system.

11 1 2000MSC : 35B65, 35Q35, 35Q8622 2 Department of Mathematics, Oklahoma State University, 401 Mathematical Sciences, Stillwater, OK 74078, USA

1. Introduction and statement of results

We study the generalized magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) system defined as follows:

{∂u∂t+(u⋅∇)u−(b⋅∇)b+∇π+νΛ2​αu=0,∂b∂t+(u⋅∇)b−(b⋅∇)u+ηΛ2​βb=0,∇⋅u=∇⋅b=0,u(x,0)=u0(x),b(x,0)=b0(x),\begin{cases}\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}+(u\cdot\nabla)u-(b\cdot\nabla)b+\nabla\pi+\nu\Lambda^{2\alpha}u=0,\\ \frac{\partial b}{\partial t}+(u\cdot\nabla)b-(b\cdot\nabla)u+\eta\Lambda^{2\beta}b=0,\\ \nabla\cdot u=\nabla\cdot b=0,\hskip 14.22636ptu(x,0)=u_{0}(x),b(x,0)=b_{0}(x),\end{cases} (1)

where u:ℝN×ℝ+↦ℝNu:\mathbb{R}^{N}\times\mathbb{R}^{+}\mapsto\mathbb{R}^{N} is the velocity vector field, b:ℝN×ℝ+↦ℝNb:\mathbb{R}^{N}\times\mathbb{R}^{+}\mapsto\mathbb{R}^{N} the magnetic vector field, π:ℝN×ℝ+↦ℝ\pi:\mathbb{R}^{N}\times\mathbb{R}^{+}\mapsto\mathbb{R} the pressure scalar field and ν,η≥0\nu,\eta\geq 0 are the kinematic viscosity and diffusivity constants respectively. We also denote by Λ\Lambda a fractional Laplacian operator defined via Fourier transform as Λ2​γ​f^​(ξ)=|ξ|2​γ​f^​(ξ)\widehat{\Lambda^{2\gamma}f}(\xi)=\lvert\xi\rvert^{2\gamma}\hat{f}(\xi) for any γ∈ℝ\gamma\in\mathbb{R}.

In case N=2,3,ν,η>0,α=β=1N=2,3,\nu,\eta>0,\alpha=\beta=1, it is well-known that (1) possesses at least one global L2L^{2} weak solution; in case N=2N=2, it is also unique (cf. [19]). Moreover, in any dimension N≥2N\geq 2, the case ν,η>0\nu,\eta>0, the lower bounds on the powers of the fractional Laplacians at α≥12+N4,β≥12+N4\alpha\geq\frac{1}{2}+\frac{N}{4},\beta\geq\frac{1}{2}+\frac{N}{4} imply the existence of the unique global strong solution pair (cf. [26]).

Some numerical study have shown that the velocity vector field may play relatively important role in regularizing effect (e.g. [8], [18]). Starting from the works of [9] and [34], we have seen various regularity criteria of the MHD system in terms of only the velocity vector field (e.g. [1], [4], [6], [7], [10], [25], [28], [33]). Moreover, motivated by the work of [20], the author in [24] showed that in case N≥2,ν,η>0,α≥12+N4,β>0N\geq 2,\nu,\eta>0,\alpha\geq\frac{1}{2}+\frac{N}{4},\beta>0 such that α+β≥1+N2\alpha+\beta\geq 1+\frac{N}{2}, the system (1) even in logarithmically super-critical case still admits a unique global strong solution pair. The endpoint case ν>0,η=0,α=1+N2\nu>0,\eta=0,\alpha=1+\frac{N}{2} was also completed recently in [23] and [29] (cf. [27] for further generalization).

On the other hand, in case N=2N=2, it is well-known that the Euler equations, the Navier-Stokes system with no dissipation, still admits a unique global strong solution. This is due to the conservation of vorticity which follows upon taking a curl on the system. In the case of the MHD system, upon taking a curl and then L2L^{2}-estimates of the resulting system, every non-linear term has bb involved. Exploiting this observation and divergence-free conditions, the authors in [2] showed that in case N=2N=2, full Laplacians in both dissipation and magnetic diffusion are not necessary for the solution pair to remain smooth; rather, only a mix of partial dissipation and diffusion in the order of two derivatives suffices.

Very recently, the authors in [22] have shown that in case N=2N=2, the solution pair remains smooth in any of the following three cases:

  1. (1)

    α≥12,β≥1\alpha\geq\frac{1}{2},\beta\geq 1,

  2. (2)

    α≥2,β=0\alpha\geq 2,\beta=0,

  3. (3)

    12>α≥0,2​α+β>2\frac{1}{2}>\alpha\geq 0,2\alpha+\beta>2.

In particular, their result implies that in the range of α∈[0,12)\alpha\in[0,\frac{1}{2}), β\beta must satisfy

β>2−2​α.\beta>2-2\alpha. (2)

These results implied that if α=0\alpha=0, then β>2\beta>2 was necessary to obtain global regularity result. This was improved in [31] to show that either of the following conditions suffices:

  1. (1)

    α=0,β>32\alpha=0,\beta>\frac{3}{2},

  2. (2)

    12>α>0,32≥β>54,α+2​β>3\frac{1}{2}>\alpha>0,\frac{3}{2}\geq\beta>\frac{5}{4},\alpha+2\beta>3.

In particular, this implies that in the range of α∈(0,12)\alpha\in(0,\frac{1}{2}), β\beta must satisfy

β>3−α2\beta>\frac{3-\alpha}{2} (3)

(cf. also [32]). In this paper we make further improvement in this direction. Let us present our results.

Theorem 1.1.

Let N=2,ν,η>0,α>13,β=1N=2,\nu,\eta>0,\alpha>\frac{1}{3},\beta=1. Then for all initial data pair (u0,b0)∈Hs​(ℝ2)×Hs​(ℝ2),s≥3(u_{0},b_{0})\in H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2})\times H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2}),s\geq 3, there exists a unique global strong solution pair (u,b)(u,b) to (1) such that

u∈C⁡([0,∞),Hs​(ℝ2))∩L2​([0,∞),Hs+α​(ℝ2)),\displaystyle u\in C([0,\infty);H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2}))\cap L^{2}([0,\infty);H^{s+\alpha}(\mathbb{R}^{2})),
b∈C⁡([0,∞),Hs​(ℝ2))∩L2​([0,∞),Hs+1​(ℝ2)).\displaystyle b\in C([0,\infty);H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2}))\cap L^{2}([0,\infty);H^{s+1}(\mathbb{R}^{2})).
Theorem 1.2.

Let N=2,ν,η>0,α∈(0,13],β∈(1,32]N=2,\nu,\eta>0,\alpha\in(0,\frac{1}{3}],\beta\in(1,\frac{3}{2}] such that

3<2​β+2​α1−α.3<2\beta+\frac{2\alpha}{1-\alpha}. (4)

Then for all initial data pair (u0,b0)∈Hs​(ℝ2)×Hs​(ℝ2),s≥3(u_{0},b_{0})\in H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2})\times H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2}),s\geq 3, there exists a unique global strong solution pair (u,b)(u,b) to (1) such that

u∈C⁡([0,∞),Hs​(ℝ2))∩L2​([0,∞),Hs+α​(ℝ2)),\displaystyle u\in C([0,\infty);H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2}))\cap L^{2}([0,\infty);H^{s+\alpha}(\mathbb{R}^{2})),
b∈C⁡([0,∞),Hs​(ℝ2))∩L2​([0,∞),Hs+β​(ℝ2)).\displaystyle b\in C([0,\infty);H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2}))\cap L^{2}([0,\infty);H^{s+\beta}(\mathbb{R}^{2})).
Remark 1.1.
  1. (1)

    We observe that (4) is equivalent to

    32−α1−α<β,\frac{3}{2}-\frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha}<\beta,

    and this is a better lower bound than that of (2) or (3) for α∈(0,13]\alpha\in(0,\frac{1}{3}].

  2. (2)

    Theorem 1.1 also represents the smaller lower bound for the sum of α+β\alpha+\beta at 1+131+\frac{1}{3} required for the solution pair to remain smooth for all time in comparison to the previous works such as [24] and [26] at α+β≥1+N2\alpha+\beta\geq 1+\frac{N}{2} in NN-dimension and [22] at α+β≥32\alpha+\beta\geq\frac{3}{2} in two-dimension.

  3. (3)

    There are various spaces of functions in which one may obtain local well-posedness of the MHD system. We chose to state above for simplicity. The local theory may be obtained by using mollifiers as done in [14] and we omit the details referring interested readers to [2] where the authors considered (1) in case N=2,ν=0,η>0,β=1N=2,\nu=0,\eta>0,\beta=1 and showed in particular the existence of its weak solution pair (cf. also [19] and [26]).

  4. (4)

    After this work was completed, this direction of research has caught much attention from many mathematicians and a remarkable development with new results has been seen. In particular, we mention that in [3] and [11], the authors obtained the global regularity result in the case α=0,β>1\alpha=0,\beta>1. We also mention numerical analysis results obtained in [21] concerning the interesting case α=0,β=1\alpha=0,\beta=1.

In the following section, let us set up notations and summarize key lemmas that will be used repeatedly. Thereafter, we prove our theorems.

3. Proof of Theorem 1.1

Throughout this section, we assume α∈(13,2−1)\alpha\in(\frac{1}{3},\sqrt{2}-1) as the case α∈[2−1,12)\alpha\in[\sqrt{2}-1,\frac{1}{2}) may be done via slight modification using Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequalities. We note that the restriction of this range of α\alpha in particular becomes crucial at (9); we chose the statements of Propositions 3.1-3.3 for simplicity of presentation. We work on

{∂tu+(u⋅∇)u−(b⋅∇)b+∇π+Λ2​αu=0,∂tb+(u⋅∇)b−(b⋅∇)u+Λ2b=0.\begin{cases}\partial_{t}u+(u\cdot\nabla)u-(b\cdot\nabla)b+\nabla\pi+\Lambda^{2\alpha}u=0,\\ \partial_{t}b+(u\cdot\nabla)b-(b\cdot\nabla)u+\Lambda^{2}b=0.\end{cases} (6)

Taking L2L^{2}-inner products of (6) with uu and bb respectively, we can get

supt∈[0,T]∥u⁡(t)∥L22+∥b⁡(t)∥L22+∫0T∥Λα​u∥L22+∥Λ​b∥L22​𝑑τ≤c⁡(u0,b0,T).\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\lVert u(t)\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert b(t)\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\int_{0}^{T}\lVert\Lambda^{\alpha}u\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert\Lambda b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}d\tau\leq c(u_{0},b_{0},T). (7)

It has been shown that the following proposition can be attained as long as β≥1\beta\geq 1 (cf. [22], [31]). We sketch its proof for completeness.

Proposition 3.1.

Let N=2,ν,η>0,α∈(13,2−1),β=1N=2,\nu,\eta>0,\alpha\in(\frac{1}{3},\sqrt{2}-1),\beta=1. Then for any solution pair (u,b)(u,b) to (1) in [0,T][0,T] there exists a constant c⁡(u0,b0,T)c(u_{0},b_{0},T) such that

supt∈[0,T]∥w⁡(t)∥L22+∥j⁡(t)∥L22+∫0T∥Λα​w∥L22+∥Λ​j∥L22​𝑑τ≤c⁡(u0,b0,T).\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\lVert w(t)\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert j(t)\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\int_{0}^{T}\lVert\Lambda^{\alpha}w\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert\Lambda j\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}d\tau\leq c(u_{0},b_{0},T).
Proof.

Taking curls on (6), we obtain

{∂tw+Λ2​αw=−(u⋅∇)w+(b⋅∇)j,∂tj+Λ2j=−(u⋅∇)j+(b⋅∇)w+2[∂1b1(∂1u2+∂2u1)−∂1u1(∂1b2+∂2b1)].\begin{cases}\partial_{t}w+\Lambda^{2\alpha}w=-(u\cdot\nabla)w+(b\cdot\nabla)j,\\ \partial_{t}j+\Lambda^{2}j=-(u\cdot\nabla)j+(b\cdot\nabla)w+2[\partial_{1}b_{1}(\partial_{1}u_{2}+\partial_{2}u_{1})-\partial_{1}u_{1}(\partial_{1}b_{2}+\partial_{2}b_{1})].\end{cases} (8)

Taking L2L^{2}-inner products with ww and jj respectively and using incompressibility of uu and bb, we estimate

12​∂t(∥w∥L22+∥j∥L22)+∥Λα​w∥L22+∥Λ​j∥L22\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\partial_{t}(\lVert w\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert j\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2})+\lVert\Lambda^{\alpha}w\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert\Lambda j\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}
=\displaystyle= 2​∫[∂1b1​(∂1u2+∂2u1)−∂1u1​(∂1b2+∂2b1)]​j\displaystyle 2\int[\partial_{1}b_{1}(\partial_{1}u_{2}+\partial_{2}u_{1})-\partial_{1}u_{1}(\partial_{1}b_{2}+\partial_{2}b_{1})]j
≲\displaystyle\lesssim ∥∇b∥L4​∥∇u∥L2​∥j∥L4\displaystyle\lVert\nabla b\rVert_{L^{4}}\lVert\nabla u\rVert_{L^{2}}\lVert j\rVert_{L^{4}}
≲\displaystyle\lesssim ∥j∥L2​∥∇j∥L2​∥w∥L2\displaystyle\lVert j\rVert_{L^{2}}\lVert\nabla j\rVert_{L^{2}}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{2}}
≤\displaystyle\leq 12​∥Λ​j∥L22+c​∥j∥L22​∥w∥L22\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\lVert\Lambda j\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+c\lVert j\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}

by Ho¨\ddot{o}lder’s, Gagliardo-Nirenberg and Young’s inequalities. Absorbing diffusive term, (7) and Gronwall’s inequality complete the proof of Proposition 3.1.

Next two propositions are the keys to the improvement from previous results:

Proposition 3.2.

Let N=2,ν,η>0,α∈(13,2−1),β=1N=2,\nu,\eta>0,\alpha\in(\frac{1}{3},\sqrt{2}-1),\beta=1. Then for any solution pair (u,b)(u,b) to (1) in [0,T][0,T], for any γ∈(1,1+α)\gamma\in(1,1+\alpha), there exists a constant c⁡(u0,b0,T)c(u_{0},b_{0},T) such that

supt∈[0,T]∥Λγ​b​(t)∥L22+∫0T∥Λ1+γ​b∥L22​𝑑τ≤c⁡(u0,b0,T).\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\lVert\Lambda^{\gamma}b(t)\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\int_{0}^{T}\lVert\Lambda^{1+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}d\tau\leq c(u_{0},b_{0},T).
Proof.

We fix γ∈(1,1+α)\gamma\in(1,1+\alpha). From the magnetic field equation of (6), we estimate after multiplying by Λ2​γ​b\Lambda^{2\gamma}b and integrating in space as follows:

12​∂t∥Λγ​b∥L22+∥Λ1+γ​b∥L22\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\partial_{t}\lVert\Lambda^{\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert\Lambda^{1+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}
≤\displaystyle\leq (∥(u⋅∇)b∥H˙γ−1∥Λ1+γb∥L2+∥(b⋅∇)u∥H˙γ−1∥Λ1+γb∥L2)\displaystyle(\lVert(u\cdot\nabla)b\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\gamma-1}}\lVert\Lambda^{1+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}+\lVert(b\cdot\nabla)u\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\gamma-1}}\lVert\Lambda^{1+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}})
≤\displaystyle\leq 12∥Λ1+γb∥L22+c(∥(u⋅∇)b∥H˙γ−12+∥(b⋅∇)u∥H˙γ−12)\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\lVert\Lambda^{1+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+c(\lVert(u\cdot\nabla)b\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\gamma-1}}^{2}+\lVert(b\cdot\nabla)u\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\gamma-1}}^{2})

by Ho¨\ddot{o}lder’s and Young’s inequalities. Now we use Lemmas 2.4 and 2.1 to estimate

∥(b⋅∇)u∥H˙γ−12≲∥b∥H˙γ−α2∥∇u∥H˙α2≲∥b∥H˙γ−α2∥w∥H˙α2.\displaystyle\lVert(b\cdot\nabla)u\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\gamma-1}}^{2}\lesssim\lVert b\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\gamma-\alpha}}^{2}\lVert\nabla u\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\alpha}}^{2}\lesssim\lVert b\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\gamma-\alpha}}^{2}\lVert w\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\alpha}}^{2}.

We then use Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality, (7) and Proposition 3.1 to further bound by

∥(b⋅∇)u∥H˙γ−12≲(∥b∥L22​(1−(γ−α))∥∇b∥L22​(γ−α))∥w∥H˙α2≲∥w∥H˙α2.\displaystyle\lVert(b\cdot\nabla)u\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\gamma-1}}^{2}\lesssim(\lVert b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2(1-(\gamma-\alpha))}\lVert\nabla b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2(\gamma-\alpha)})\lVert w\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\alpha}}^{2}\lesssim\lVert w\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\alpha}}^{2}.

Next, we fix ϵ∈(0,1−α)\epsilon\in(0,1-\alpha) and estimate

∥(u⋅∇)b∥H˙γ−12\displaystyle\lVert(u\cdot\nabla)b\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\gamma-1}}^{2} ≲\displaystyle\lesssim ∥u∥H˙γ−1+ϵ2​∥∇b∥H˙1−ϵ2\displaystyle\lVert u\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\gamma-1+\epsilon}}^{2}\lVert\nabla b\rVert_{\dot{H}^{1-\epsilon}}^{2}
≲\displaystyle\lesssim ∥u∥L22​(2−γ−ϵ)​∥u∥H˙12​(γ−1+ϵ)​∥j∥H˙1−ϵ2≲∥j∥L22​ϵ​∥j∥H˙12​(1−ϵ)≲(1+∥j∥H˙12)\displaystyle\lVert u\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2(2-\gamma-\epsilon)}\lVert u\rVert_{\dot{H}^{1}}^{2(\gamma-1+\epsilon)}\lVert j\rVert_{\dot{H}^{1-\epsilon}}^{2}\lesssim\lVert j\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2\epsilon}\lVert j\rVert_{\dot{H}^{1}}^{2(1-\epsilon)}\lesssim(1+\lVert j\rVert_{\dot{H}^{1}}^{2})

by Lemma 2.4, Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequalities, Lemma 2.1, Proposition 3.1 and Young’s inequality. Thus, absorbing diffusive term, we have

∂t∥Λγ​b∥L22+∥Λ1+γ​b∥L22≲(∥w∥H˙α2+1+∥j∥H˙12).\partial_{t}\lVert\Lambda^{\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert\Lambda^{1+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}\lesssim(\lVert w\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\alpha}}^{2}+1+\lVert j\rVert_{\dot{H}^{1}}^{2}).

Hence, by Proposition 3.1, integrating in time we obtain

supt∈[0,T]∥Λγ​b​(t)∥L22+∫0T∥Λ1+γ​b∥L22​𝑑τ≤c⁡(u0,b0,T).\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\lVert\Lambda^{\gamma}b(t)\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\int_{0}^{T}\lVert\Lambda^{1+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}d\tau\leq c(u_{0},b_{0},T).

This completes the proof of Proposition 3.2.

Proposition 3.3.

Let N=2,ν,η>0,α∈(13,2−1),β=1N=2,\nu,\eta>0,\alpha\in(\frac{1}{3},\sqrt{2}-1),\beta=1. Then for any solution pair (u,b)(u,b) to (1) in [0,T][0,T], for any γ∈(1,1+α)\gamma\in(1,1+\alpha), there exists a constant c⁡(u0,b0,T)c(u_{0},b_{0},T) such that

Proposition 4.2.

Let N=2,ν,η>0,α∈(0,13],β∈(1,32]N=2,\nu,\eta>0,\alpha\in(0,\frac{1}{3}],\beta\in(1,\frac{3}{2}] satisfy (10). Then for any solution pair (u,b)(u,b) to (1) in [0,T][0,T], for any γ∈(β,α+β)\gamma\in(\beta,\alpha+\beta), there exists a constant c⁡(u0,b0,T)c(u_{0},b_{0},T) such that

supt∈[0,T]∥Λγ​b​(t)∥L22+∫0T∥Λβ+γ​b∥L22​𝑑τ≤c⁡(u0,b0,T).\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\lVert\Lambda^{\gamma}b(t)\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\int_{0}^{T}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}d\tau\leq c(u_{0},b_{0},T).
Proof.

We fix γ∈(β,α+β)\gamma\in(\beta,\alpha+\beta). From the magnetic field equation of (11), we estimate after multiplying by Λ2​γ​b\Lambda^{2\gamma}b and integrating in space

12​∂t∥Λγ​b∥L22+∥Λβ+γ​b∥L22\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\partial_{t}\lVert\Lambda^{\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert\Lambda^{\beta+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}
≤\displaystyle\leq (∥(u⋅∇)b∥H˙γ−β∥Λβ+γb∥L2+∥(b⋅∇)u∥H˙γ−β∥Λβ+γb∥L2)\displaystyle(\lVert(u\cdot\nabla)b\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\gamma-\beta}}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}+\lVert(b\cdot\nabla)u\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\gamma-\beta}}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}})
≤\displaystyle\leq 12∥Λβ+γb∥L22+c(∥(u⋅∇)b∥H˙γ−β2+∥(b⋅∇)u∥H˙γ−β2)\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+c(\lVert(u\cdot\nabla)b\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\gamma-\beta}}^{2}+\lVert(b\cdot\nabla)u\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\gamma-\beta}}^{2})

by Ho¨\ddot{o}lder’s and Young’s inequalities. Now by Lemma 2.4 and Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality, Lemma 2.1 and Proposition 4.1, we estimate

∥(b⋅∇)u∥H˙γ−β≲∥b∥H˙γ−β+1−α2∥∇u∥H˙α2≲∥b∥L22​(α+β−γ)∥∇b∥L22​(1−(α+β−γ))∥w∥H˙α2≲∥w∥H˙α2.\displaystyle\lVert(b\cdot\nabla)u\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\gamma-\beta}}\lesssim\lVert b\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\gamma-\beta+1-\alpha}}^{2}\lVert\nabla u\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\alpha}}^{2}\lesssim\lVert b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2(\alpha+\beta-\gamma)}\lVert\nabla b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2(1-(\alpha+\beta-\gamma))}\lVert w\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\alpha}}^{2}\lesssim\lVert w\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\alpha}}^{2}.

Next, we fix ϵ∈(β−1,β−α)\epsilon\in(\beta-1,\beta-\alpha) and estimate using Lemma 2.4 and Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequalities, (12), Proposition 4.1 and Young’s inequality as follows:

∥(u⋅∇)b∥H˙γ−β2\displaystyle\lVert(u\cdot\nabla)b\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\gamma-\beta}}^{2} ≲\displaystyle\lesssim ∥u∥H˙γ+1−2​β+ϵ2​∥∇b∥H˙β−ϵ2\displaystyle\lVert u\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\gamma+1-2\beta+\epsilon}}^{2}\lVert\nabla b\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\beta-\epsilon}}^{2}
≲\displaystyle\lesssim ∥u∥L22​(2​β−γ−ϵ)​∥∇u∥L22​(1−(2​β−γ−ϵ))​∥j∥H˙β−ϵ2\displaystyle\lVert u\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2(2\beta-\gamma-\epsilon)}\lVert\nabla u\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2(1-(2\beta-\gamma-\epsilon))}\lVert j\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\beta-\epsilon}}^{2}
≲\displaystyle\lesssim ∥j∥L22​(ϵβ)​∥j∥H˙β2​(1−ϵβ)≲1+∥j∥H˙β2.\displaystyle\lVert j\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2(\frac{\epsilon}{\beta})}\lVert j\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\beta}}^{2(1-\frac{\epsilon}{\beta})}\lesssim 1+\lVert j\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\beta}}^{2}.

Therefore, we have shown

12​∂t∥Λγ​b∥L22+∥Λβ+γ​b∥L22≤12​∥Λβ+γ​b∥L22+c⁡(∥w∥H˙α2+1+∥j∥H˙β2).\frac{1}{2}\partial_{t}\lVert\Lambda^{\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert\Lambda^{\beta+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}\leq\frac{1}{2}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+c(\lVert w\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\alpha}}^{2}+1+\lVert j\rVert_{\dot{H}^{\beta}}^{2}).

Integrating in time and using Proposition 4.1 complete the proof of Proposition 4.2.

Proposition 4.3.

Let N=2,ν,η>0,α∈(0,13],β∈(1,32]N=2,\nu,\eta>0,\alpha\in(0,\frac{1}{3}],\beta\in(1,\frac{3}{2}] satisfy (10). Then for any solution pair (u,b)(u,b) to (1) in [0,T][0,T], for any γ∈(β,α+β)\gamma\in(\beta,\alpha+\beta), there exists a constant c⁡(u0,b0,T)c(u_{0},b_{0},T) such that

supt∈[0,T]∥w⁡(t)∥L2​(1+α)3−β−γ2​(1+α)3−β−γ+∫0T∥w∥L2​(1+α)(3−β−γ)​(1−α)2​(1+α)3−β−γ​𝑑τ≤c⁡(u0,b0,T).\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\lVert w(t)\rVert_{L^{\frac{2(1+\alpha)}{3-\beta-\gamma}}}^{\frac{2(1+\alpha)}{3-\beta-\gamma}}+\int_{0}^{T}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{\frac{2(1+\alpha)}{(3-\beta-\gamma)(1-\alpha)}}}^{\frac{2(1+\alpha)}{3-\beta-\gamma}}d\tau\leq c(u_{0},b_{0},T).
Proof.

We fix γ∈(β,α+β)\gamma\in(\beta,\alpha+\beta) and denote

p=2​(1+α)3−β−γp=\frac{2(1+\alpha)}{3-\beta-\gamma}

Note due to (10), we have 3−β−γ>03-\beta-\gamma>0. We estimate by multiplying the vorticity equation of (13) by |w|p−2​w\lvert w\rvert^{p-2}w and integrating in space, using Lemma 2.3 and the same homogeneous Sobolev embedding of H˙α↪L21−α\dot{H}^{\alpha}\hookrightarrow L^{\frac{2}{1-\alpha}} as before to obtain

1p​∂t∥w∥Lpp+c⁡(p,α)​∥w∥Lp1−αp≤∥b∥L∞​∥∇j∥Lp1+α​∥w∥Lpp−2​∥w∥Lp1−α\displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\partial_{t}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{p}}^{p}+c(p,\alpha)\lVert w\rVert_{L^{\frac{p}{1-\alpha}}}^{p}\leq\lVert b\rVert_{L^{\infty}}\lVert\nabla j\rVert_{L^{\frac{p}{1+\alpha}}}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{p}}^{p-2}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{\frac{p}{1-\alpha}}}

by Ho¨\ddot{o}lder’s inequality. By our choice of pp, we see that we may continue our estimate by

1p​∂t∥w∥Lpp+c⁡(p,α)​∥w∥Lp1−αp\displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\partial_{t}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{p}}^{p}+c(p,\alpha)\lVert w\rVert_{L^{\frac{p}{1-\alpha}}}^{p}
≤\displaystyle\leq ∥b∥L∞​∥∇j∥L23−β−γ​∥w∥Lpp−2​∥w∥Lp1−α\displaystyle\lVert b\rVert_{L^{\infty}}\lVert\nabla j\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{3-\beta-\gamma}}}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{p}}^{p-2}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{\frac{p}{1-\alpha}}}
≲\displaystyle\lesssim ∥b∥L2γ−1γ​∥Λγ​b∥L21γ​∥Λβ+γ​b∥L2​∥w∥Lpp−2​∥w∥Lp1−α\displaystyle\lVert b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma}}\lVert\Lambda^{\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1}{\gamma}}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{p}}^{p-2}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{\frac{p}{1-\alpha}}}
≤\displaystyle\leq c⁡(p,α)2​∥w∥Lp1−αp+c⁡(∥Λβ+γ​b∥L22+1)​(∥w∥Lpp+1)\displaystyle\frac{c(p,\alpha)}{2}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{\frac{p}{1-\alpha}}}^{p}+c(\lVert\Lambda^{\beta+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+1)(\lVert w\rVert_{L^{p}}^{p}+1)

where we used the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality, homogeneous Sobolev embedding of H˙β+γ−2↪L23−β−γ\dot{H}^{\beta+\gamma-2}\hookrightarrow L^{\frac{2}{3-\beta-\gamma}}, Propositions 4.1 and 4.2, Young’s inequalities.

Absorbing dissipative term, Gronwall’s inequality and Proposition 4.2 complete the proof of Proposition 4.3.

Proposition 4.4.

Let N=2,ν,η>0,α∈(0,13],β∈(1,32]N=2,\nu,\eta>0,\alpha\in(0,\frac{1}{3}],\beta\in(1,\frac{3}{2}] satisfy (10). Then for any solution pair (u,b)(u,b) to (1) in [0,T][0,T], there exists a constant c⁡(u0,b0,T)c(u_{0},b_{0},T) such that

supt∈[0,T]∥∇w(t)∥L22+∥∇j(t)∥L22+∫0T∥Λα∇w∥L22+∥Λβ∇j∥L22dτ≤c(u0,b0,T).\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\lVert\nabla w(t)\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert\nabla j(t)\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\int_{0}^{T}\lVert\Lambda^{\alpha}\nabla w\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}\nabla j\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}d\tau\leq c(u_{0},b_{0},T).
Proof.

Similarly as before, we apply ∇\nabla on (13), take L2L^{2}-inner products with ∇w,∇j\nabla w,\nabla j respectively to estimate

12∂t(∥∇w(t)∥L22+∥∇j(t)∥L22)+∥Λα∇w∥L22+∥Λβ∇j∥L22\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\partial_{t}(\lVert\nabla w(t)\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert\nabla j(t)\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2})+\lVert\Lambda^{\alpha}\nabla w\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}\nabla j\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}
=\displaystyle= −∫∇w⋅∇u⋅∇wdx−∫∇j⋅∇u⋅∇jdx\displaystyle-\int\nabla w\cdot\nabla u\cdot\nabla wdx-\int\nabla j\cdot\nabla u\cdot\nabla jdx
+∫∇((b⋅∇)j)⋅∇w+∇((b⋅∇)w)⋅∇jdx\displaystyle+\int\nabla((b\cdot\nabla)j)\cdot\nabla w+\nabla((b\cdot\nabla)w)\cdot\nabla jdx
+2∫∇[∂1b1(∂1u2+∂2u1)]⋅∇jdx−2∫∇[∂1u1(∂1b2+∂2b1)]⋅∇jdx=∑i=15Ii.\displaystyle+2\int\nabla[\partial_{1}b_{1}(\partial_{1}u_{2}+\partial_{2}u_{1})]\cdot\nabla jdx-2\int\nabla[\partial_{1}u_{1}(\partial_{1}b_{2}+\partial_{2}b_{1})]\cdot\nabla jdx=\sum_{i=1}^{5}I_{i}.

As before,

I1≤∥∇w∥L2∥∇u∥L2α∥∇w∥L21−α≤18∥Λα∇w∥L22+cY(t)∥w∥L2α2\displaystyle I_{1}\leq\lVert\nabla w\rVert_{L^{2}}\lVert\nabla u\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{\alpha}}}\lVert\nabla w\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{1-\alpha}}}\leq\frac{1}{8}\lVert\Lambda^{\alpha}\nabla w\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+cY(t)\lVert w\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{\alpha}}}^{2}

by Ho¨\ddot{o}lder’s inequality, homogeneous Sobolev embedding of H˙α↪L21−α\dot{H}^{\alpha}\hookrightarrow L^{\frac{2}{1-\alpha}} and Young’s inequalities. Next,

I2≤∥∇j∥L42∥∇u∥L2≲∥∇j∥L22​(2​β−12​β)∥Λβ∇j∥L22​(12​β)≤18∥Λβ∇j∥L22+cY(t)\displaystyle I_{2}\leq\lVert\nabla j\rVert_{L^{4}}^{2}\lVert\nabla u\rVert_{L^{2}}\lesssim\lVert\nabla j\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2(\frac{2\beta-1}{2\beta})}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}\nabla j\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2(\frac{1}{2\beta})}\leq\frac{1}{8}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}\nabla j\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+cY(t)

by Ho¨\ddot{o}lder’s inequality, Proposition 4.1, Gagliardo-Nirenberg and Young’s inequalities. Next, we estimate I3I_{3} after same integration by parts in the proof of Proposition 3.4,

I3\displaystyle I_{3} ≲\displaystyle\lesssim (∥∇j∥L42​∥w∥L2+∥∇b∥L2β−1​∥Δ​j∥L22−β​∥w∥L2)\displaystyle(\lVert\nabla j\rVert_{L^{4}}^{2}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{2}}+\lVert\nabla b\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{\beta-1}}}\lVert\Delta j\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{2-\beta}}}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{2}})
≲\displaystyle\lesssim ∥∇j∥L22​(2​β−12​β)∥Λβ∇j∥L22​(12​β)+∥∇b∥L22​β+γ−3β+γ−1∥Λβ+γb∥L22−ββ+γ−1∥Λβ∇j∥L2\displaystyle\lVert\nabla j\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2(\frac{2\beta-1}{2\beta})}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}\nabla j\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2(\frac{1}{2\beta})}+\lVert\nabla b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{2\beta+\gamma-3}{\beta+\gamma-1}}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{2-\beta}{\beta+\gamma-1}}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}\nabla j\rVert_{L^{2}}
≤\displaystyle\leq 18∥Λβ∇j∥L22+c(Y(t)+1+∥Λβ+γb∥L22)\displaystyle\frac{1}{8}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}\nabla j\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+c(Y(t)+1+\lVert\Lambda^{\beta+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2})

by Ho¨\ddot{o}lder’s and Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequalities, homogeneous Sobolev’s embedding of H˙β−1↪L22−β\dot{H}^{\beta-1}\hookrightarrow L^{\frac{2}{2-\beta}} and Proposition 4.1.

The estimates of I4I_{4} and I5I_{5} are simple: after the same integration by parts as before, we have

I4+I5≲∫|∇b|​|∇u|​|Δ​j|​𝑑x≲∥∇b∥L2β−1​∥Δ​j∥L22−β​∥w∥L2\displaystyle I_{4}+I_{5}\lesssim\int\lvert\nabla b\rvert\lvert\nabla u\rvert\lvert\Delta j\rvert dx\lesssim\lVert\nabla b\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{\beta-1}}}\lVert\Delta j\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{2-\beta}}}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{2}}

by Ho¨\ddot{o}lder’s inequality and hence the same estimate as the second term of I3I_{3} suffices. In sum, after absorbing dissipative and diffusive terms, we have

∂tY(t)+∥Λα∇w∥L22+∥Λβ∇j∥L22≲(Y(t)+1)(1+∥w∥L2α2+∥Λβ+γb∥L22).\displaystyle\partial_{t}Y(t)+\lVert\Lambda^{\alpha}\nabla w\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}\nabla j\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}\lesssim(Y(t)+1)(1+\lVert w\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{\alpha}}}^{2}+\lVert\Lambda^{\beta+\gamma}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}).

Now we see that we may choose γ=3−β−α⁡(1+α)1−α\gamma=3-\beta-\frac{\alpha(1+\alpha)}{1-\alpha} so that

β<γ<α+β\beta<\gamma<\alpha+\beta (14)

due to (10) and therefore, by Ho¨\ddot{o}lder’s inequality we have

∫0T∥w∥L2α2​𝑑τ≤Tβ+γ−2+α1+α​(∫0T∥w∥L2​(1+α)(3−β−γ)​(1−α)2​(1+α)3−β−γ​𝑑τ)3−β−γ1+α≤c⁡(u0,b0,T)\int_{0}^{T}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{\alpha}}}^{2}d\tau\leq T^{\frac{\beta+\gamma-2+\alpha}{1+\alpha}}\left(\int_{0}^{T}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{\frac{2(1+\alpha)}{(3-\beta-\gamma)(1-\alpha)}}}^{\frac{2(1+\alpha)}{3-\beta-\gamma}}d\tau\right)^{\frac{3-\beta-\gamma}{1+\alpha}}\leq c(u_{0},b_{0},T)

due to Proposition 4.3. Thus, Gronwall’s inequality and Proposition 4.2 complete the proof of Proposition 4.4.

Proof of Theorem 1.2

We are now ready to complete the proof of Theorem 1.2. Similarly as before we apply Λs,s∈ℝ+\Lambda^{s},s\in\mathbb{R}^{+} on (11) and take L2L^{2}-inner products with Λs​u\Lambda^{s}u and Λs​b\Lambda^{s}b respectively to estimate using Lemma 2.2

∂t(∥Λs​u∥L22+∥Λs​b∥L22)+∥Λs+α​u∥L22+∥Λs+β​b∥L22\displaystyle\partial_{t}(\lVert\Lambda^{s}u\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert\Lambda^{s}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2})+\lVert\Lambda^{s+\alpha}u\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert\Lambda^{s+\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}
≲\displaystyle\lesssim ∥∇u∥L2α​∥Λs​u∥L2​∥Λs​u∥L21−α\displaystyle\lVert\nabla u\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{\alpha}}}\lVert\Lambda^{s}u\rVert_{L^{2}}\lVert\Lambda^{s}u\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{1-\alpha}}}
+(∥∇u∥L21−α∥Λs−1∇b∥L2α+∥Λsu∥L21−α∥∇b∥L2α)∥Λsb∥L2\displaystyle+(\lVert\nabla u\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{1-\alpha}}}\lVert\Lambda^{s-1}\nabla b\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{\alpha}}}+\lVert\Lambda^{s}u\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{1-\alpha}}}\lVert\nabla b\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{\alpha}}})\lVert\Lambda^{s}b\rVert_{L^{2}}
+∥∇b∥L2α​∥Λs​b∥L2​∥Λs​u∥L21−α\displaystyle+\lVert\nabla b\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{\alpha}}}\lVert\Lambda^{s}b\rVert_{L^{2}}\lVert\Lambda^{s}u\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{1-\alpha}}}
+(∥∇b∥L2α∥Λs−1∇u∥L21−α+∥Λsb∥L2α∥∇u∥L21−α)∥Λsb∥L2\displaystyle+(\lVert\nabla b\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{\alpha}}}\lVert\Lambda^{s-1}\nabla u\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{1-\alpha}}}+\lVert\Lambda^{s}b\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{\alpha}}}\lVert\nabla u\rVert_{L^{\frac{2}{1-\alpha}}})\lVert\Lambda^{s}b\rVert_{L^{2}}
≲\displaystyle\lesssim ∥w∥L2α​∥∇w∥L21−α​∥Λs​u∥L2​∥Λs+α​u∥L2\displaystyle\lVert w\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\alpha}\lVert\nabla w\rVert_{L^{2}}^{1-\alpha}\lVert\Lambda^{s}u\rVert_{L^{2}}\lVert\Lambda^{s+\alpha}u\rVert_{L^{2}}
+(∥Λαw∥L2∥Λsb∥L2α+β−1β∥Λs+βb∥L21−αβ+∥Λs+αu∥L2∥∇b∥L2α∥∇∇b∥L21−α)∥Λsb∥L2\displaystyle+(\lVert\Lambda^{\alpha}w\rVert_{L^{2}}\lVert\Lambda^{s}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{\alpha+\beta-1}{\beta}}\lVert\Lambda^{s+\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1-\alpha}{\beta}}+\lVert\Lambda^{s+\alpha}u\rVert_{L^{2}}\lVert\nabla b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\alpha}\lVert\nabla\nabla b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{1-\alpha})\lVert\Lambda^{s}b\rVert_{L^{2}}
+∥∇b∥L2α∥∇∇b∥L21−α∥Λsb∥L2∥Λs+αu∥L2\displaystyle+\lVert\nabla b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\alpha}\lVert\nabla\nabla b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{1-\alpha}\lVert\Lambda^{s}b\rVert_{L^{2}}\lVert\Lambda^{s+\alpha}u\rVert_{L^{2}}
+(∥∇b∥L2α∥∇∇b∥L21−α∥Λs+αu∥L2+∥Λsb∥L2α+β−1β∥Λs+βb∥L21−αβ∥Λα∇u∥L2)∥Λsb∥L2\displaystyle+(\lVert\nabla b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\alpha}\lVert\nabla\nabla b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{1-\alpha}\lVert\Lambda^{s+\alpha}u\rVert_{L^{2}}+\lVert\Lambda^{s}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{\alpha+\beta-1}{\beta}}\lVert\Lambda^{s+\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1-\alpha}{\beta}}\lVert\Lambda^{\alpha}\nabla u\rVert_{L^{2}})\lVert\Lambda^{s}b\rVert_{L^{2}}
≲\displaystyle\lesssim ∥Λs​u∥L2​∥Λs+α​u∥L2\displaystyle\lVert\Lambda^{s}u\rVert_{L^{2}}\lVert\Lambda^{s+\alpha}u\rVert_{L^{2}}
+∥w∥L21−α​∥∇w∥L2α​∥Λs​b∥L2α+2​β−1β​∥Λs+β​b∥L21−αβ+∥Λs+α​u∥L2​∥Λs​b∥L2\displaystyle+\lVert w\rVert_{L^{2}}^{1-\alpha}\lVert\nabla w\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\alpha}\lVert\Lambda^{s}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{\alpha+2\beta-1}{\beta}}\lVert\Lambda^{s+\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1-\alpha}{\beta}}+\lVert\Lambda^{s+\alpha}u\rVert_{L^{2}}\lVert\Lambda^{s}b\rVert_{L^{2}}
+∥Λs​b∥L2​∥Λs+α​u∥L2\displaystyle+\lVert\Lambda^{s}b\rVert_{L^{2}}\lVert\Lambda^{s+\alpha}u\rVert_{L^{2}}
+∥Λs​b∥L2α+2​β−1β​∥Λs+β​b∥L21−αβ​∥w∥L21−α​∥∇w∥L2α\displaystyle+\lVert\Lambda^{s}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{\alpha+2\beta-1}{\beta}}\lVert\Lambda^{s+\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1-\alpha}{\beta}}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{2}}^{1-\alpha}\lVert\nabla w\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\alpha}
≤\displaystyle\leq 12​(∥Λs+α​u∥L22+∥Λs+β​b∥L22)+c⁡(∥Λs​u∥L22+∥Λs​b∥L22)\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\left(\lVert\Lambda^{s+\alpha}u\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert\Lambda^{s+\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}\right)+c(\lVert\Lambda^{s}u\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert\Lambda^{s}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2})

by Ho¨\ddot{o}lder’s inequalities, Lemma 2.1, homogeneous Sobolev embedding of H˙α↪L21−α\dot{H}^{\alpha}\hookrightarrow L^{\frac{2}{1-\alpha}} and Gagliardo-Nirenberg and Young’s inequalities. Absorbing the dissipative and diffusive terms, Gronwall’s inequality complete the proof of Theorem 1.2.
